links.outcome: Classification accuracy with versus without control of acquisition-related metadata confounders in two CT datasets
links.effect: Controlling for identified confounding factors increased classification accuracy by 5 to 15% compared to datasets where these factors remained uncontrolled.
links.quote: Empirical evaluation in two distinct CT datasets demonstrates that controlling for factors identified by our method drastically improves model performance, increasing classification accuracy by 5 to 15% compared to datasets where these factors remain uncontrolled.

unlisted_practices: Unsupervised automated detection of confounding metadata attributes in imaging datasets before model training

screen.reason: Evaluates an unsupervised method for detecting metadata confounders to improve robustness and prevent model drift across CT imaging datasets, comparing model performance with and without controlling for these identified factors.
